Returning to Lobby releases all scene-local player cameras. Camera rect layouts are deterministic; the sample does not add dynamic Split Screen transitions or camera collision.

docs.title: Rocket Rumble Menus, Settings and Lifecycle
docs.text: This guide covers the shared behavior of Rocket Rumble 2D and Rocket Rumble 3D, optional 2–4-player sample games. Keep this folder when using either sample. Begin with Quick Start for framework setup; these menus and match rules are sample content.

docs.title: Main Menu and lobby
docs.text:
Open the chosen sample's Main Menu scene and enter Play Mode. PLAY opens its lobby; SETTINGS contains Audio and Controls; QUIT exits a standalone build and leaves Editor Play Mode running. Main Menu creates no joined players.

Join with Q, P, gamepad Start or a matched joystick's Join control. Browse and confirm Cobalt, Ember, Mint or Orchid, then move focus down to START GAME. At least two joined players must be Ready with available input. Moving focus does not clear Ready. The default lobby controls are independent of gameplay bindings.

Menu panels support mouse, keyboard, gamepad and configured joystick navigation. Keyboard A uses WASD/F, Keyboard B arrows/Enter; gamepads use stick/D-pad/South; the supplied DragonRise profile uses stick/button2. Visible Back controls and keyboard G/Backspace/Escape or controller/profile Cancel return to the preceding panel. Couch focus and navigation manages selection recovery, scopes and modals. Release held controls before the next fresh menu press.

docs.title: Audio settings
docs.text:
Master, Music, SFX and UI sliders apply immediately to the included sample mixer. Zero mutes; 100% is 0 dB. Defaults are Master 100%, Music about 25%, SFX about 56% and UI about 45%. RESET AUDIO DEFAULTS restores and saves them. Sample audio preferences use PlayerPrefs and survive scene changes/restarts; they are separate from input profiles.

One persistent sample audio service carries lobby music through menu/settings/lobby. Countdown has no arena music; GO starts arena music; victory stops it; lobby return restores lobby music. Jump, death, respawn, rocket launch, countdown, winner and UI feedback use included sample audio. The service releases itself when leaving Rocket Rumble scenes. This is sample audio integration, not a required framework audio system.

docs.title: Controls settings
docs.text:
Choose Keyboard A, Keyboard B, a connected gamepad family or a configured Joystick profile. The device-less gamepad placeholder can show/reset defaults but CHANGE needs connected hardware. Gameplay rows cover Move, Jump, Fire, Shield and Pause / Winner Return. Lobby Confirm/Back/Leave are fixed, separate controls; Join is not offered for rebinding.

Bindings belong to Input Binding Profiles, never P1–P4 seats. KeyboardA/KeyboardB follow their logical roles; controller settings follow the resolved family/profile. Identical controllers without verified unique identity share settings, while keeping separate actions, sessions and InputUsers. Seat reuse cannot transfer another source's profile. See Input Binding Profiles for the storage abstraction and honest identity fallback.

Select CHANGE, then provide a control from the chosen device. Keyboard captures reserve Escape for cancellation. Gamepad and joystick captures do not reserve their normal UI Cancel button: East/Circle/B and the joystick profile Cancel control remain gameplay binding candidates, subject to normal conflicts. Click the visible CANCEL button to abort, or wait for the ten-second timeout; waiting also provides cancellation without mouse or keyboard. UI navigation/Submit/Back are suspended while capturing. Other devices cannot choose/cancel that capture through their input controls. After capture, release held controls; focus returns to the Change button. Conflicting different actions in one gameplay map and Keyboard A/B overlap are rejected without changing the save. Separate controller devices may reuse equivalent buttons; lobby/UI maps may reuse gameplay controls.

The stock samples keep Share/View as a fixed Leave control during gameplay. Avoid assigning it to Fire or another gameplay action: the current gameplay conflict validator does not include that separate Leave map, so an accepted override also causes Drop Out. This collision is a known follow-up; ordinary controller Back/Cancel candidates are not reserved by the capture operation.

  • A row's RESET resets that profile/action; a Move reset restores all its parts.
  • RESET PROFILE resets the selected source's profile after confirmation.
  • RESET ALL CONTROLS clears all saved framework profiles after separate confirmation.

The sample uses the framework JSON store at Application.persistentDataPath/CouchCoopBuilder/input-bindings.json; customers can substitute IInputBindingProfileStore. Unreadable saves disable editing rather than silently overwriting data. Overrides conflicting with changed defaults require correction/reset; unmatched old binding addresses remain unapplied. Settings previews create no fake players or InputUsers.

docs.title: Pause and Device Lost
docs.text:
The shared Pause panel reads each player's owned Pause action: defaults T / Y / Start / DragonRise button11. Joined players with available input can navigate using their existing lobby controls; mouse also works. Pause is available during countdown and gameplay; the Winner screen owns its separate return flow.

Pause sets Time.timeScale to zero, freezing physics, projectiles, scoring, countdown and respawn timers. Music/gameplay SFX pause; UI audio continues. Resume restores the same voices and timers. Movement, Jump, Fire and Shield require neutral controls followed by fresh input; shield cooldown is retained. Scene exit restores time.

Physical Device Lost auto-pauses and retains the session, representation and score. The panel identifies unavailable seats. Device regain/reclaim clears the warning but does not resume automatically; Resume remains blocked while required input is missing. Replacement-device ambiguity follows the framework's reserved-controller recovery policy, with no invented cross-launch identity.

RETURN TO LOBBY keeps sessions, Player Index values and selected characters, including disconnected reservations. Ready and match score reset for the next round. MAIN MENU permanently ends all sessions; the next PLAY begins with zero joined players. Saved audio preferences and input profiles remain.

docs.title: Drop Out and Rejoin
docs.text:
In an active match, the owned Leave control (G / Backspace / Select / DragonRise button12) requests reversible Drop Out. The session, Player Index, character, score, InputUser and profile remain reserved. The sample releases the representation and gameplay action clone, removes that player's rockets, and displays DROPPED OUT / PRESS JOIN TO RETURN. Survivors continue; Drop Out causes no death/score or automatic win.

The same role/controller's normal Join restores that session with a new selected-character representation at a safe authored spawn. Shield resets Ready; held gameplay controls need fresh input. Dropping out while dead cancels pending respawn. If everyone voluntarily drops out, ALL PLAYERS LEFT / PRESS JOIN TO RETURN pauses the arena; the first valid Join restores play. DeviceRegained alone does not reverse voluntary Drop Out.

This differs from Device Lost, which keeps the representation, and explicit permanent TryLeave, which releases the session/seat. See framework lifecycle APIs when integrating your own game.

docs.title: What to study and adapt
docs.text:
Shared components implement authored menu panels, audio preferences, profile editing, Pause, lobby feedback and safe-point selection. They consume public framework APIs without creating another ownership model. Both games use Gameplay Player Setup for spawning and Gameplay Player Binding for isolated owned actions. Movement, combat, score, respawn, camera follow and match policy belong to the samples.

Test your copy with supported hardware: navigate settings without mouse, edit/reset a profile, return lobby/game, Drop Out/Rejoin a middle player, and test actual Device Lost separately. Surviving Player Index/session mappings should stay stable. These examples are local sample games, not networking, arbitrary-game camera controllers or performance guarantees.

docs.title: Sample index
docs.text:
Before entering Play Mode, use Configure Supplied Samples for Rocket Rumble and Persistent Sessions. Split Screen Playgrounds run independently. Customize customer-owned copies rather than supplied assets.

Sample / capacity Open Study Rocket Rumble 2D, 2–4 Main Menu (Assets/LevelArgento/CouchCoopBuilder/Samples/RocketRumble2D/Scenes/RocketRumble2DMainMenu.unity) Platform combat, owned actions, settings, reversible Drop Out/Rejoin; fixed Shared Camera Rocket Rumble 3D, 2–4 Main Menu (Assets/LevelArgento/CouchCoopBuilder/Samples/RocketRumble3D/Scenes/RocketRumble3DMainMenu.unity) XZ combat, the same profile/settings flow, optional individual views and runtime Camera Settings Split Screen Playgrounds, 1–8 3D (Assets/LevelArgento/CouchCoopBuilder/Samples/SplitScreenPlaygrounds/Scenes/SplitScreenPlayground3D.unity) / 2D (Assets/LevelArgento/CouchCoopBuilder/Samples/SplitScreenPlaygrounds/Scenes/SplitScreenPlayground2D.unity) Direct join/entry, camera providers/follow examples, selectable 2P/3P and automatic 4–8 layouts Supplied lobby templates, up to 4 visual slots Copy a style with the Wizard Authored panels, shared stage or carousel, previews, independent focus and one shared Start Existing Canvas example, 2 authored roots ExistingCanvasLobby (Assets/LevelArgento/CouchCoopBuilder/Samples/ExistingCanvas/ExistingCanvasLobby.unity) Explicit UI references and reuse; author more roots for up to eight Persistent sessions example, 4 PersistentLobbyPrototype (Assets/LevelArgento/CouchCoopBuilder/Prototypes/Persistent/PersistentLobbyPrototype.unity) Identity/selection across lobby/game return; scene-local Ready

The gameplay context examples can create an eight-capacity input bootstrap when opened standalone; standalone joining does not select a character automatically. To demonstrate selected-character spawning, enter through a configured lobby with confirmed selections. Use the sample host's Return to Origin Lobby (Play Mode) context action to return. None of these diagnostic examples supplies general movement or game rules.

Related guides: Character Catalog and Previews, Gameplay Integration, Input Binding Profiles, Split Screen Cameras, Built-in Focus and Navigation.

docs.title: Gameplay examples
docs.text:
The sample index links every entry scene. Context examples support eight sessions and show ownership in the Inspector; they have no movement or match rules:

Example What to study API Only (Assets/LevelArgento/CouchCoopBuilder/Samples/Gameplay/GameplayApiOnly.unity) Public contexts without representation bindings Existing Objects (Assets/LevelArgento/CouchCoopBuilder/Samples/Gameplay/GameplayExistingObjects.unity) Eight authored indexed objects; the inactive P8 object stays inactive Custom Provider (Assets/LevelArgento/CouchCoopBuilder/Samples/Gameplay/GameplayCustomProvider.unity) Indexed provider, one resolution per session per enabled cycle Explicit Spawn Points (Assets/LevelArgento/CouchCoopBuilder/Samples/Gameplay/GameplaySpawnPoints.unity) Eight indexed poses, selected Gameplay Prefabs and framework clone ownership Origin + Offset (Assets/LevelArgento/CouchCoopBuilder/Samples/Gameplay/GameplaySpawnOriginOffset.unity) Rotated formation and owned-input diagnostics on resolved clones Custom Placement (Assets/LevelArgento/CouchCoopBuilder/Samples/Gameplay/GameplaySpawnCustomPlacement.unity) A placement provider returning poses without creating objects

For selected-character handoff, use your own saved lobby, assign a valid catalog, target the chosen scene on PersistentScenePrototype and enable both scenes in the scene list used by the active Build Profile. Join/confirm, Start Game, inspect the context/binding, then use Return to Origin Lobby (Play Mode) on the sample host. Selection/session identity persists; Ready resets. The scenes can create an eight-capacity bootstrap when opened standalone, but Join alone does not select a character; spawning needs a confirmed selection.

Origin + Offset demonstrates the generic gameplay defaults: A WASD/IJKL/F/R/Space/T; B arrows/numpad look/Enter/Right Shift/numpad 0/Y; gamepads left stick or D-pad/right stick/South/East/West/Start, for Move/Look/Primary/Secondary/Jump/Pause respectively. Generic joysticks use their configured profile. These defaults differ from Rocket Rumble's sample controls. PlayerInputSampleCapsule is an authored example of the disabled UnityEvent bridge described above; it is not required for other strategies.

When adapting a sample, check independent input, Leave/rejoin of a middle seat, device loss and repeated lobby returns. Surviving indexes/users stay stable; each new scene gets fresh scene-owned bindings. See Chapter 20 — Troubleshooting and the isolated ResolutionFailed/InputBindingFailed diagnostic when configuration is missing.

docs.title: Device Lost, Drop Out and Rejoin
Reserved controller replacement during a session
docs.text:
Same-instance InputUser.DeviceLost / DeviceRegained preserves the user, session, context, binding and representation. Gamepad/joystick services follow the regained owned device, including a replacement instance with the same runtime ID.

For a genuinely new device ID, Unity does not generate DeviceRegained by matching hardware descriptions. The framework can reclaim the existing user's reserved seat:

  • Automatic reclaim requires one unavailable owner with the exact same nonempty product, layout and full device description, including a nonempty serial unique among the known controller owners.
  • Without a serial, pressing the normal Join action can explicitly reclaim exactly one matching reserved seat. This is seat-reclaim intent, not proof of physical identity.
  • The incoming device must have appeared after loss; controllers already registered when the loss occurred keep their ordinary Join semantics.
  • Multiple matching reserved seats are ambiguous: reclaim and duplicate Join are rejected. Reconnect the original instances, or intentionally end those sessions.
  • Differing or missing hardware descriptions are not guessed. Display-name suffixes and deviceId are never persistent identities. No cross-launch identity is claimed.

Reclaim clears only the existing user's obsolete lost pairing and pairs its replacement through InputUser. It does not create another session, user or gameplay object. Device Disabled/Enabled also updates controller availability; both shared keyboard roles report availability from their existing user's live paired keyboard.

docs.title: Optional gameplay Drop Out and Rejoin
docs.text:
MultiplayerCoordinator.TryLeave(sessionId) remains a permanent Leave: it removes the session, releases its input slot, InputUser and scene binding, and allows the lowest available PlayerIndex to be reused. A gameplay scene can opt into reversible owned Leave actions by setting coordinator.DropOutOnLeave = true for that scene's lifetime and restoring false on teardown. The shared keyboard, gamepad and joystick services then route their owned Leave callbacks through TryHandleLeaveRequest.

Drop Out keeps the PlayerSession, InputSlot, PlayerIndex, selected character and input role/profile reservation. PlayerSession.IsDroppedOut and GameplayPlayerContext.IsDroppedOut distinguish it from DeviceLost; IsInputAvailable returns false for dropped-out gameplay. PlayerDroppedOut / PlayerRejoined events also reach GameplayPlayerContexts. GameplayPlayerSetup releases its scene binding on Drop Out and resolves the selected character again on rejoin. It does not choose a sample respawn point or preserve a game's score; those are scene-owned decisions. The matching input service accepts the normal Join control for the exact still-owned keyboard role or connected controller instance and calls TryRejoin without creating a new PlayerSession or InputUser. Device replacement still follows the conservative metadata-based reclaim policy above; ambiguous hardware is not guessed. An automatic DeviceRegained does not itself reactivate a voluntarily dropped-out participant.

TryDropOut and TryRejoin are explicit APIs for integrations that have validated the relevant input source. An explicit TryLeave remains permanent even while the opt-in owned-action policy is enabled. Main Menu shutdown uses permanent Leave. The opt-in flag is scene policy; customers should set it only where their gameplay represents dropped-out players and reset it when that scene ends.

docs.title: Scene handoff and authority
docs.text:
CouchCoopBootstrap preserves MultiplayerCoordinator, joined PlayerSession instances, character-selection IDs and the input services across scene transitions when its lifetime is PersistAcrossScenes. Those services retain the actual session InputUsers and actions. PersistentScenePrototype remembers the origin lobby and loads a selected gameplay scene; returning reconstructs scene presenters. Ready is scene-local and resets; character selection persists until explicit Leave.

The Setup Wizard selects a gameplay scene and configures the persistent transition. Configure gameplay representations and input separately on that scene’s components; the Wizard does not choose a resolution mode, author spawn points, or configure input adapters. Its optional Cameras step works with an existing Gameplay Player Setup. Selection previews instantiate presentation content separately from gameplay.

GameplayPlayerContext references the authoritative session. The bootstrap-owned GameplayPlayerContexts collection is a read-only projection, not another session store. It retains no scene gameplay objects.

docs.title: Public access
docs.text:
After initializing your bootstrap, access bootstrap.GameplayPlayers. Code without an injected bootstrap can use CouchCoopBootstrap.Active explicitly:

using LevelArgento.CouchCoopBuilder;

CouchCoopBootstrap bootstrap = CouchCoopBootstrap.Active;
if (bootstrap != null && bootstrap.IsInitialized &&
    bootstrap.GameplayPlayers.TryGetPlayer(0, out GameplayPlayerContext player))
{
    int index = player.PlayerIndex;                  // Zero-based, 0 through 7.
    System.Guid sessionId = player.SessionId;       // Stable until Leave.
    string selectedId = player.SelectedCharacterId;
    CharacterDefinition character = player.CharacterDefinition;
    if (player.TryGetInputUser(out var user))
    {
        // Consume existing ownership; do not pair a new user here.
        foreach (var device in user.pairedDevices) { /* Your integration. */ }
    }
}

P1–P8 are one-based UI labels for zero-based PlayerIndex values 0–7. InputSlot identifies the input role/source; it is not a persistent controller or binding-profile identity. Saved input overrides belong to Input Binding Profiles, never a reusable PlayerIndex.

Lookup accepts either PlayerIndex or session Guid. Players is ordered by ascending PlayerIndex and may contain gaps after Leave: list position is not necessarily PlayerIndex. A returning controller after intentional Leave receives a new session at the lowest available index under the existing policy. Surviving contexts, IDs and indexes do not move. Cache a context for the lifetime of that session, not for an assumed permanent controller player number.

InputUser is the existing user, never a new pairing. PairedDevices reports current pairing; Keyboard A and B have distinct users but intentionally share the keyboard device. Read IsJoined and IsInputAvailable separately: a disconnected controller can reserve a joined session while input is unavailable. An ended session exposes an invalid default InputUser. Re-read pairing/availability when needed; do not retain a snapshot as proof of connection or use inactivity as disconnection evidence.

CharacterDefinition resolves the selected ID against the current configured catalog only if that ID has one match. It does not require GameplayPrefab. CharacterStatus distinguishes no selection, resolved metadata and unresolved metadata. TryGetCharacterDefinition(out definition, out failureMessage) explains missing catalogs, missing IDs and ambiguity. Missing metadata does not invalidate session/input ownership or block custom resolution. API-only mode produces no configuration errors for absent objects or character metadata.

Built-in lobby selection requires a fully valid catalog, including Gameplay Prefabs. Context metadata lookup is independent of that lobby rule. The built-in Spawn Selected Character strategy requires the selected definition to have GameplayPrefab; Existing Objects, Custom Provider and API Only do not check that requirement.

Selected Character IDs and session ownership persist across lobby/gameplay scene changes. Ready belongs to the current lobby UI. Intentional Leave ends a session; physical Device Lost keeps its reservation. Advanced recovery and reversible Drop Out rules are explained in Session Lifecycle.

docs.title: Setup Wizard
docs.text: New to Couch Co-op Builder? Begin with Chapter 2 — Requirements, Installation and Quick Start. This guide explains setup actions, saving and reruns, then points to concrete examples. Player capacity is explained in Player scope; default lobby controls are in Chapter 2.

docs.title: Setup Wizard
docs.text:
Open Tools > LevelArgento > Couch Co-op Builder > Setup Wizard. Its six steps are Start, Characters, Lobby UI, Gameplay, Cameras, Review, followed by completion.

Step What to choose / provide Start Create New Lobby copies supplied authored UI; Integrate Existing Canvas wires your saved UI. No setup preset is saved. Characters A nonempty Character Catalog, stable unique Character IDs, and Maximum Local Players. Generate from Prefabs... opens the generator; assign the resulting catalog afterward. Lobby UI New Lobby: Individual Panels, Shared Stage or Character Carousel, an existing Assets folder and a new Lobby Asset Name. Existing Canvas: assign authored controls as described in Chapter 5 — Lobby Templates and Existing Canvas. Gameplay Saved Gameplay Scene, enabled in the project scene list. The current Wizard button Add Gameplay Scene to Build Settings registers it immediately through EditorBuildSettings.scenes; this changes project scene configuration, not the scene asset. Use Open Gameplay Scene Additively and Select Gameplay Player Setup in Inspector for representation configuration. Gameplay input is a separate choice on each Gameplay Player Binding. Cameras Optional Enable Shared / Split Screen Camera Management. Assign your gameplay setup and camera source; choose 2P/3P layouts. 4–8 are automatic. See Split Screen Cameras. Review Correct blocking errors; inspect paths, scene wiring, asset saves and project scene-list changes, then Apply Setup.

The built-in character-selection lobby requires a catalog that passes Run Catalog Validation, including Gameplay Prefabs. The Wizard can show a missing-prefab warning without blocking Apply; that warning does not mean lobby confirmation will work. Assign those prefabs before testing character selection. API-only gameplay metadata lookup has a separate, looser contract; see Gameplay Integration.

docs.title: Outputs and completion
docs.text:
Create New Lobby copies the chosen authored prefab to your output folder and creates a scene using that editable copy. It assigns catalog/capacity/destination, disables unused supplied slots, and registers the lobby in the project scene list. Source templates remain unchanged. Existing scene/prefab paths are never overwritten. Choose an existing folder under Assets using Browse...; create your own folder in the Project window first if needed.

Integrate Existing Canvas wires required references and adds/reuses nonvisual services, input contexts and previews. It preserves authored positions, fonts, colors, sprites and layout. The lobby scene is marked dirty, not automatically saved. Optional camera wiring also marks the gameplay scene dirty; save it after Apply. Missing/duplicate required references and wrong-scene/hierarchy assignments are reported before applying.

Completion lists the applied workflow, capacity/catalog, lobby/gameplay paths and integration choices. Use Open Lobby Scene, save, then Test Lobby in Play Mode; the test action is enabled only when that lobby is active. Select the catalog or the copied prefab when customizing content. Open gameplay and follow Chapter 7 — Gameplay Representation and Spawning and Chapter 8 — Gameplay Input Integration to supply your game-owned objects, movement and input. Confirm all joined players and test shared Start and return to the originating lobby.

Scene wiring supports Edit > Undo. Created disk assets and project scene-list registration are separate saved changes, not guaranteed to reverse with scene Undo. Review identifies any operation that saves other dirty assets. Failed New Lobby creation removes its own partial outputs.

docs.title: Run setup again
docs.text:
Start Another Setup clears only temporary Wizard choices. It does not remove previous scenes/assets. A new lobby needs a new name/folder. To update a configured lobby, choose Existing Canvas, assign its Canvas, and review the suggested player bindings; explicit catalog/capacity choices are preserved. Reapplying reuses bound services, EventSystems and preview contexts and deduplicates project scene-list registration. To extend capacity, author additional complete roots, raise Maximum Local Players and bind the new entries before applying.

Legacy Text and TextMeshPro (TMP) are separate assignments: use one implementation per label. Optional labels/graphics may remain empty. TMP labels need an authored font asset; the Wizard does not install or change Unity packages.

Figure 1. The Characters step assigns a catalog and maximum capacity. Scene UI design remains authored.

docs.title: Split Screen Playgrounds
docs.text: These 1–8-player camera examples complement Quick Start. Open SplitScreenPlayground3D (Assets/LevelArgento/CouchCoopBuilder/Samples/SplitScreenPlaygrounds/Scenes/SplitScreenPlayground3D.unity) or SplitScreenPlayground2D (Assets/LevelArgento/CouchCoopBuilder/Samples/SplitScreenPlaygrounds/Scenes/SplitScreenPlayground2D.unity) and enter Play Mode. These independent scenes use URP and the installed Input System and built-in Couch UI navigation. Their lightweight join screen needs no separate lobby scene, Rocket Rumble content or Cinemachine. They are not automatically registered in the project's scene configuration; add the chosen scene to the scene list used by your active Build Profile when building a sample.

docs.title: Try it
docs.text:
1. Join with Q (Keyboard A), P (Keyboard B), or a controller's Start. The authored 4x2 grid shows eight equally sized P1-P8 cards with waiting/joined state and input source. Up to eight real input sources may join; the two keyboard roles share one physical keyboard. There is no Ready requirement.
  2. Select ENTER PLAYGROUND with F (Keyboard A), Enter (Keyboard B), a controller profile's Confirm (south face button on standard gamepads), or a mouse click. One through eight joined players may enter. Existing representations, contexts and InputUsers are retained; gameplay movement/settings yield to the join screen until entry.
  3. Move with WASD, arrow keys, or the controller stick. Jump with Space, numpad 0, or the gamepad's west face button (X on Xbox / Square on PlayStation). These scenes use the framework's default gameplay bindings.
  4. Open Camera Settings with Tab, its mouse button, or a joined player's Pause binding (T / Y / Start). The Split Screen control receives focus. Player movement yields while the panel is open; world physics continues.
  5. Use up/down to select and left/right to change. Keyboard A uses W/S, A/D, F; Keyboard B uses arrows, Enter; gamepads use stick/D-pad, south face button. Mouse arrows and Back also work. Close with Escape, gamepad east, or Back. Layout rows are hidden while Split Screen is OFF.
  6. Toggle Shared -> Split -> Shared -> Split. Change both two-player layouts and all four three-player layouts. Camera settings are scene-local and begin with Split Screen OFF (shared view), two-player Vertical, and Top 2 / Bottom 1.
  7. Drop out with G / Backspace / controller Select. Rejoin with the same source's Q / P / Start. Drop Out reserves the original session and PlayerIndex; it destroys that sample representation and recreates it at its spawn on rejoin. It is distinct from temporary DeviceLost, which retains the representation and view.

Configured generic joysticks use their GenericControllerProfile controls. The scene bootstrap includes the existing DragonRise profile; add other recognized profiles to its Shared Joystick Input list. Matching/pairing and gameplay binding resolution remain framework responsibilities.

docs.title: Integration to read
docs.text:
• PlaygroundSessionProvider implements public IGameplayPlayerProvider and supplies a simple authored prefab per context to GameplayPlayerSetup. It owns representation creation/destruction, eight spawn transforms, participant collision exclusions and palette. Sessions, InputUsers and input actions are provided by the framework.
  • PlaygroundJoinPanel reads existing contexts for eight authored cards and invokes the authored Enter button from each player's owned Confirm action. It creates no sessions/devices/InputUsers. The join panel is the only navigation owner while visible; settings yield until entry. Spawns use two clear 3D plaza rows and eight non-overlapping 2D floor positions.
  • PlaygroundCameraSettings calls public GameplayCameraManager.SetSplitScreenEnabled, SetTwoPlayerLayout and SetThreePlayerLayout. One settings router reads the existing owned menu actions. Couch focus and navigation manages focus recovery; the UI module handles pointers only, with no second move/submit/cancel router. All visible controls and HUD are saved in the scenes.
  • The manager owns assignment, camera lifetime, active viewport packing and the single AudioListener policy. Both scenes use its camera-prefab source and the same default layout provider. Active PlayerIndex values pack in ascending order even when there are gaps.
  • PlaygroundFollowCamera3D reads its public GameplayCameraAssignment.Representation, follows smoothly with a fixed 45-degree heading, and uses a little more distance for narrow viewports. Its perspective prefab is independent of player facing. Shared 3D uses a fixed authored high-angle overview that covers the usable playground.
  • PlaygroundCamera2D supplies orthographic behavior. Individual cameras follow the assigned representation; the shared camera frames the active group using the public setup lookup. Follow size, maximum shared size and simple level bounds are inspector settings. Extreme separation zooms the shared view out rather than tethering players.
  • PlaygroundPlayer3D / PlaygroundPlayer2D read only their own GameplayPlayerBinding.Input. They demonstrate move, grounded jump and facing. Falling below the sample floor returns the same representation to its spawn; there is no combat, score, health or full game loop.

The follow scripts are sample implementations. GameplayCameraManager does not require these behaviors. Replace them with your project's camera behavior while keeping the public assignment.

docs.title: Presentation and limits
docs.text:
The 3D deck has four color districts, a central plaza, stepped terraces, ramps, a bridge and modest obstacles. The 2D stage has four districts, increasing platform heights and small floor gaps. Player colors and compact P1-P8 markers match the framework conventions.

See the authoritative 1–8 layout table for selectable 2P/3P and automatic 4–8 arrangements. Viewport badges use one-based P1–P8 labels for the actual zero-based PlayerIndex, not the packed viewport number. The header and Camera Settings stay global above the cameras.

Eight cameras render the scene eight times. Small viewports reduce detail/readability and increase rendering cost. This sample has one unshadowed directional light in 3D, unlit materials in 2D, no post-processing and no particles. Profile your own content and target hardware. Shared overview players can be small; the 3D follow example has no occlusion avoidance or camera collision rig, so geometry can briefly obscure a player. The 2D bounds limit empty edges in individual views; an extremely wide shared view necessarily shows space outside the vertical level.

docs.title: Try your integration
docs.text:
Join the player count your game supports, enter, and toggle Shared/Split Screen. Confirm each view follows its owning representation and only one assigned-camera AudioListener is active. Test two-/three-player choices and automatic four-/five-/six-/seven-/eight-player layouts. Drop Out a middle player: views pack by ascending PlayerIndex without renumbering the surviving sessions. Rejoin the same source, test actual Device Lost separately, then exit Play Mode and check for teardown errors.

Customize your own copies of the saved scenes and prefabs directly. These examples demonstrate camera integration, not a complete game or a promise of camera framing/performance for every level.

docs.title: Shared and Split Screen Cameras
docs.text: Quick Start covers setup; Player scope explains capacity. This guide describes optional camera integration.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
GameplayCameraManager is an optional, scene-local module for shared and individual player cameras, with built-in Split Screen layouts for 1-8 local players. It manages camera assignment, rendering state and Camera.rect.

You own camera behavior. The framework does not prescribe follow, orbit, aim, chase, zoom, collision or multiple-target framing. Your camera prefab or provider can contain your own behavior. The Playground and Rocket Rumble cameras are sample implementations, not universal camera controllers.

Configure gameplay players normally first; see Chapter 7 — Gameplay Representation and Spawning. The manager requires a GameplayPlayerSetup that resolves representations. If your game creates its own objects, use that setup's existing Custom Provider mode with an IGameplayPlayerProvider returning those objects. HandleItMyself does not resolve representations for camera management.

No camera module is required for input, sessions, selection or gameplay integration. Cinemachine is not required.

docs.title: 2. Shared vs Split Screen
docs.text:
• Split Screen OFF: your Shared Camera renders the full screen; assigned individual cameras stop rendering.
  • Split Screen ON: individual cameras render for active resolved participants; the Shared Camera stops rendering. If no individual camera can be resolved, Shared remains a fallback when available.

Changing mode preserves PlayerSession identity, PlayerIndex, InputUser, selected character and gameplay representation. It does not reload scenes or recreate gameplay players. Switching back to Shared requires a Shared Camera reference.

docs.title: 3. Setup Wizard quick start
docs.text:
1. Configure your gameplay scene's GameplayPlayerSetup and representation source, then save the scene.
  2. Open Tools > LevelArgento > Couch Co-op Builder > Setup Wizard. Choose the lobby workflow, catalog, capacity and gameplay scene normally.
  3. On the Cameras step, check Enable Shared / Split Screen Camera Management. It is unchecked by default. Unchecked means no manager is added, no camera fields are required, and existing camera setup is left untouched.
  4. Use Open Gameplay Scene Additively to load the chosen gameplay scene alongside the lobby. Assign its Gameplay Player Setup; the Wizard suggests it only when exactly one candidate exists. Assign your existing Shared Camera from that scene.
  5. Choose Camera Prefab, Camera On Gameplay Representation, or Custom Provider, with the source described below. Prefab/provider configuration is required even when the initial mode is Shared, so runtime Split switching has a usable source.
  6. Choose Default Camera Mode: Shared / Split, the two-player layout and the three-player layout. Four through eight use automatic built-in layouts. Advanced options allow an existing custom layout provider and an AudioListener policy.
  7. Complete the authored lobby/Canvas bindings. On Review, inspect validation and the plan, then Apply Setup. The Wizard adds one GameplayCameraManager on the assigned setup object if none exists, or reuses the single existing manager in the gameplay scene. It assigns references and defaults, without creating camera objects or providers.
  8. Save the gameplay scene after Apply, and save the lobby for Existing Canvas. The gameplay scene is marked dirty, not automatically saved. Enter Play Mode, join players and call SetSplitScreenEnabled(true) from your Settings UI.

Existing Canvas lobby and camera edits form one scene Undo operation. New Lobby output assets cannot be deleted by scene Undo; camera wiring still supports Undo. Project scene-list additions are a separate project-configuration effect. New Lobby refuses to overwrite existing output assets and removes partial outputs if creation fails.

Rerunning reads the single existing manager's configuration when you assign the setup object or open its scene through the Wizard. Review those suggested references before Apply. Reapplying reconciles one manager, without duplicate cameras or providers. Multiple managers produce an actionable validation error rather than a guess about which one to replace. Turning the checkbox off leaves any previously configured manager intact.

docs.title: 4. Manual setup
docs.text:
1. Add GameplayCameraManager to the gameplay scene, normally on the GameplayPlayerSetup object.
  2. Assign Player Setup, your Shared Camera, and Player Camera Source with its prefab/provider where applicable.
  3. Set Split Screen Enabled, Two Player Layout, Three Player Layout, and optionally the layout provider/audio policy in the Inspector.
  4. Author camera behavior and test both modes with real joined gameplay participants.

For code-driven setup, use Configure(GameplayPlayerSetup setup, Camera shared, GameplayCameraSource source, GameObject prefab = null, IGameplayCameraProvider provider = null). It releases the previous camera assignment cycle. Settings toggles should use SetSplitScreenEnabled instead of repeatedly calling Configure.

docs.title: 5. Runtime toggle and layouts
docs.text:
These are independent Settings actions; cameraManager is your assigned GameplayCameraManager reference. Include using LevelArgento.CouchCoopBuilder; in scripts using these types:

cameraManager.SetSplitScreenEnabled(true);  // Split
cameraManager.SetSplitScreenEnabled(false); // Shared

cameraManager.SetTwoPlayerLayout(TwoPlayerViewportLayout.Vertical);
cameraManager.SetThreePlayerLayout(ThreePlayerViewportLayout.TopTwoBottomOne);

Read state through SplitScreenEnabled, TwoPlayerLayout and ThreePlayerLayout. The Wizard default is serialized scene configuration; your Settings UI can change it at runtime. The module does not persist preferences or generate a mandatory Settings screen.

Public event Use SplitScreenModeChanged (Action<bool>) Reflect Shared/Split changes in your Settings UI. ViewportLayoutChanged (Action) React after rect/rendering-state changes, including layout and participant updates. PlayerCameraAssigned (Action<GameplayPlayerContext, Camera, GameObject>) Connect camera behavior or HUD to its current context and representation.

Subscribe/unsubscribe with your component's normal lifecycle. TryGetPlayerCamera(int playerIndex, out Camera camera) finds an assigned active camera. Call Refresh() after an unavailable custom camera becomes ready to retry assignment.

docs.title: 6. Built-in layouts 1-8
docs.text:
Active views pack in ascending existing PlayerIndex order. Packing never renumbers sessions: P1 / P4 / P7 remain P1 / P4 / P7, occupying three visual slots. Unity rect coordinates start at the bottom-left; row names below describe the visual top row first.

Players Layout 1 Full screen 2 Horizontal (top/bottom) or Vertical (left/right) 3 Top 2 / Bottom 1; Bottom 2 / Top 1; Left 1 / Right 2; Right 1 / Left 2 4 2 + 2 5 3 + 2 6 3 + 3 7 4 + 3 8 4 + 4

Two- and three-player layouts are selectable; four through eight use automatic arrangements. In the automatic 4–8 arrangements, rows share screen height equally and columns fill each row. Rects cover the full screen without decorative gaps. Three-player enum values are TopTwoBottomOne, BottomTwoTopOne, LeftOneRightStack, and RightOneLeftStack. Two-player values are Horizontal and Vertical.

docs.title: Camera Prefab
docs.text:
Assign a prefab containing exactly one Camera, on the root or a child. The manager clones the full prefab once per resolved session when Split first needs it. Follow/zoom scripts on the rig are retained. No particular genre, follow script or Cinemachine package is required.

GameplayCameraAssignment is added to the clone root. Its Context and Representation identify the player and target; AssignmentChanged fires when bindings change, including rejoin. Author prefab AudioListeners disabled under the default framework policy to avoid transient duplicate listeners during cloning.

docs.title: Camera On Gameplay Representation
docs.text: Each resolved representation provides a Camera in its hierarchy. Ownership stays with its owner. The Wizard checks known authored existing objects and selected-character gameplay prefabs for missing Cameras. Dynamic/custom providers are not rejected merely because future cameras cannot be inspected: verify their resolved representations in Play Mode. A representation Camera cannot also be the Shared Camera.

docs.title: Custom Provider
docs.text:
Assign your gameplay-scene MonoBehaviour implementing IGameplayCameraProvider. Its existing method is:

bool TryResolveCamera(GameplayPlayerContext context, GameObject representation,
    out Camera camera, out string failureMessage);

Return a live scene Camera for that participant, not a prefab asset or a Camera assigned to another participant. The provider owns camera lifetime, behavior and pooling. The Wizard assigns your component; it does not invent an implementation. Multi-camera rigs/advanced stacks need your own setup through this source.

docs.title: 8. Camera ownership
docs.text:
The manager never deletes or reparents your Shared Camera, replaces follow scripts, or edits camera FOV, projection, clipping planes, renderer settings or behavior. At runtime it controls assigned cameras' enabled state and rects; the default audio policy also manages assigned-hierarchy listeners. Prior customer enabled/rect/listener states are restored on release.

Framework-created prefab clones belong to the manager. Customer representation/provider cameras stay customer-owned and are never destroyed by the manager. Disabling/destroying the manager releases its clones and restores customer state. A pooled provider should recycle cameras through its own representation lifecycle; the manager does not own that pool.

docs.title: 9. Drop Out / Rejoin and permanent Leave
docs.text:
Intentional gameplay Drop Out releases that participant's representation and removes its active viewport; remaining views repack without renumbering PlayerIndex. Rejoin restores the participant. Framework-owned camera clones remain disabled/reserved for the session and are reused with the new representation binding.

Representation cameras follow their representation's lifetime. Custom providers manage their returned cameras. Permanent Leave performs normal session cleanup and destroys framework-owned clones for that session; it is distinct from reversible Drop Out.

docs.title: 10. DeviceLost
docs.text: Temporary device loss leaves the participant represented and its camera normally assigned. The manager follows representation lifecycle, not raw device events or inactivity. Your game may pause or show reconnection UI according to its existing session policy. DeviceLost does not silently become Leave or Drop Out.

docs.title: 11. AudioListener
docs.text:
Default ManageAssignedCameraListeners enables one listener among assigned player rigs: the first active rig with a listener, or Shared as fallback. Shared mode uses the shared listener. Prior listener states are restored on release.

Only listeners in assigned player rigs/representation hierarchies and the shared-camera hierarchy are managed. Other scene listeners remain yours. The Wizard creates no extra listeners and changes no prefab assets. Select Developer Managed (DeveloperManaged) if your game owns listener switching; SetAudioPolicy(GameplayCameraAudioPolicy policy) also changes policy at runtime. Neither policy prevents duplicate listeners you independently enable elsewhere.

docs.title: 12. UI / HUD
docs.text:
• Screen Space Overlay: global full-screen UI, appropriate for Pause, Settings and Winner. It is not cropped into player viewports.
  • Screen Space Camera: an individual HUD can target its assigned Camera through Canvas.worldCamera.
  • World Space: normal Unity behavior through relevant cameras.

Subscribe to PlayerCameraAssigned to connect your authored HUD to the camera using the provided context and representation. Rebind when assignments change. The manager does not automatically clone customer HUDs. Packed visual positions are not new player identities.

docs.title: 13. URP and Cinemachine
docs.text:
Normal URP Base Cameras support Camera.rect. Overlay stacks, renderers, post-processing and renderer features remain customer-controlled. Prefab source expects exactly one Camera; use a custom provider for multi-camera stacks and verify them on your target Unity/URP version.

Cinemachine is not required. There is no Cinemachine package dependency or built-in integration package. Developers may use Cinemachine in their own prefabs/providers; its target binding and advanced URP/stack configuration remain theirs.

docs.title: 14. Custom layout provider
docs.text:
In Advanced Camera Options or the Inspector, assign an existing scene component implementing ICameraViewportLayoutProvider. Empty uses built-in layouts. At runtime use SetViewportLayoutProvider(ICameraViewportLayoutProvider provider); null returns to the built-in provider.

The interface fills normalized rects in ascending active PlayerIndex order:

bool TryGetViewports(int viewCount, TwoPlayerViewportLayout twoPlayer,
    ThreePlayerViewportLayout threePlayer, Rect[] viewports);

The manager validates finite, positive, in-bounds, non-overlapping full-screen tiling and falls back to built-in layouts if custom output is invalid. The supported range is 1-8. The Wizard checks the component/interface reference; it does not execute customer layout code during setup.

docs.title: 15. Performance
docs.text: One through eight layouts are supported. More cameras increase rendering cost; performance depends on resolution, scene complexity, shadows, post-processing, renderer features and hardware. Eight cameras do not guarantee high-setting performance on every device. Profile your own content/build and tune effects and resolution. No universal game performance is promised.

docs.title: 16. Samples
docs.text:
See the Samples index for entry points.

Demonstration Purpose Rocket Rumble 3D Real game integration, fixed Shared Camera, individual 3D follow cameras, runtime Camera Settings and Drop Out/Rejoin; up to four players. Split Screen Playground 3D Independent 1-8 join/entry flow, perspective follow cameras and 5/6/7/8 layouts. Split Screen Playground 2D Independent 1-8 join/entry flow, orthographic cameras, simple platformer movement and Shared/Split switching.

The Playground guide links both entry scenes and explains the independent 1–8-player join flow. Sample follow/framing belongs to the game; the core has no dependency on those scripts.

docs.title: 17. Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Problem Check Camera fields missing in Wizard Enable Shared / Split Screen Camera Management on the Cameras step. Cannot assign gameplay references Open the selected saved gameplay scene additively and assign its Gameplay Player Setup. Lobby objects and prefab assets are not gameplay-scene references. Shared mode has no view Assign Shared Camera; switching to Shared needs it even if initial mode was Split. Split has no individual cameras Resolve representations first and configure a camera source. HandleItMyself does not resolve objects. Camera Prefab rejected Assign an asset with exactly one Camera, including inactive children. Missing/multiple Cameras or scene objects are unusable for this source. Representation lacks a Camera Add it, choose prefab source, or use a custom provider. Test dynamically created representations after resolution. Custom provider missing/invalid Assign a live gameplay-scene component implementing IGameplayCameraProvider or ICameraViewportLayoutProvider, as applicable. Multiple managers on rerun Reconcile them explicitly; the Wizard does not delete one or guess which to configure. Duplicate AudioListener warning Disable unrelated scene listeners, author prefab listeners disabled, and verify the selected policy. HUD fills screen Overlay is global; bind an individual Screen Space Camera Canvas to its assigned camera. P numbers seem out of order after Drop Out Views repack; PlayerIndex stays stable. P1/P4/P7 still identify those sessions. Camera does not follow Supply your behavior and bind targets through GameplayCameraAssignment or PlayerCameraAssigned.

ValidateConfiguration(out string failure) reports the first basic runtime configuration problem. Detailed resolution diagnostics are reported once per problem; Refresh() can retry a provider after its camera becomes available. Fix legitimate diagnostics rather than repeatedly clearing them. No proximity split/merge, animated/diagonal splits, HUD cloning, minimap or spectator system is provided.

Keep Character IDs stable. The built-in lobby selection requires a valid catalog with Gameplay Prefabs, even if your gameplay uses existing/custom objects. Too few player panels Supplied visuals have four slots, or authored roots are missing Use Existing Canvas with one complete root per configured player, or reduce the supplied-lobby capacity. Controller does not join Capacity is full/reserved, device is unavailable, or its layout/profile does not match Check Unity Input Debugger, the assigned profile and its Join binding. A profile-matched HID must expose the required controls. Identical display names are not device identity. See device recovery. Start Game unavailable A joined player is not Ready, input is unavailable, or no player is joined Confirm each player; reconnect reserved input or intentionally Leave that session. Check the target scene is enabled in the scene list used by the active Build Profile. Existing Canvas cannot apply Required assignments, hierarchy boundaries or saved scene are missing Use each Player panel entry; assign fields marked * and resolve listed errors. Optional labels/graphics can stay empty. Gameplay has no player objects/input API-only mode is selected, representation references are missing, or no input mode is configured Configure Gameplay Player Setup and Gameplay Player Binding, or consume GameplayPlayers through your own integration. Follow the isolated runtime diagnostic. Split Screen has no views/follow Representations or a camera source/follow script are missing Resolve gameplay objects, assign the camera prefab/representation/provider, and supply follow behavior. See Chapter 10 — Shared and Split Screen Cameras. UI focus is absent EventSystem or owned UI context is inactive Check the assigned EventSystem, active scope, valid default selection and per-player input module. See Focus and Navigation.
